questions.text: Which French subject pronoun means «we»?

feedback: Vous means you (plural or polite)

questions.solution: Nous means we; vous is you (plural or polite) and ils/elles mean they
questions.hint: Its verb forms usually end in -ons

questions.text: What does «ne ... jamais» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.always: Always is toujours; ne ... jamais is a negative

questions.solution: Ne ... jamais means never, e.g. je ne mange jamais de viande = I never eat meat
questions.hint: It is the negative opposite of toujours

questions.text: What does «ne ... rien» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Ne ... rien means nothing, e.g. je ne fais rien = I do nothing / I don't do anything
questions.hint: It is the negative opposite of quelque chose

questions.text: Give the «je» form of «être» in the present tense. Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Être: je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont
questions.hint: Être is irregular: think of how you say «I am» in French

questions.text: Give the «ils» form of «avoir» in the present tense. Type the verb only.

feedback.sont: Sont comes from être (ils sont = they are); this question asks for avoir

questions.solution: Avoir: j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont
questions.hint: Avoir is irregular; this form has just three letters

questions.text: Which word means «the» before a plural noun such as «livres»?

feedback: Des means some or any, not the

questions.solution: Les is the plural definite article: les livres = the books (des means some)
questions.hint: Le and la are only used with singular nouns

questions.text: Which word means «my» before a feminine singular noun such as «sœur»?

feedback: Mon is for masculine nouns (or feminine nouns starting with a vowel)
Ta means your

questions.solution: Ma sœur = my sister; mon is for masculine nouns, mes is plural and ta means your
questions.hint: Sœur is feminine and singular

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «___ maison est grande.»

feedback: Maison is feminine, so le is wrong
Un is masculine; maison is feminine

questions.solution: Maison is feminine and singular, so it takes la: la maison est grande
questions.hint: Is maison masculine or feminine? Singular or plural?

questions.text: Which phrase is correct for «a little girl»?
questions.solution: Fille is feminine, so the article and the adjective are both feminine: une petite fille
questions.hint: Fille is feminine: check both the article and the adjective

questions.text: Translate into French. Include the definite article (le, la, l' or les): the school

feedback.la école: Before a vowel, la shortens to l'
feedback.le école: Before a vowel, le and la shorten to l'

questions.solution: École is feminine, but before a vowel la shortens to l': l'école
questions.hint: The French noun starts with a vowel

questions.text: Give the plural of «le cheval», with its article.

feedback.les chevals: Most nouns ending in -al change to -aux in the plural

questions.solution: Nouns ending in -al usually change to -aux in the plural: le cheval, les chevaux
questions.hint: Nouns ending in -al have an irregular plural, like le journal → les journaux

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Je vais ___ cinéma.»

feedback: Cinéma is masculine, so à la is wrong
Aux is used with plural nouns

questions.solution: Cinéma is masculine, and à + le becomes au: je vais au cinéma
questions.hint: Cinéma is masculine and singular; what happens when à meets le?

questions.text: Complete with the word for «my»: «___ amie s'appelle Léa.» Type the missing word only.

feedback.ma: Before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, French uses mon (mon amie)

questions.solution: Amie is feminine but starts with a vowel, so French uses mon: mon amie
questions.hint: Amie begins with a vowel sound

questions.text: Choose the correct adjective: «Mes sœurs sont ___.» (tall)
questions.solution: Sœurs is feminine plural, so add -e and -s: grandes
questions.hint: Sœurs is feminine and plural

questions.text: What does «Je ne mange jamais de viande» mean?

options: I am not eating meat today
I eat a lot of meat

questions.solution: Ne ... jamais = never, so: I never eat meat
questions.hint: Look at the negative around the verb

questions.text: What does «Nous allons regarder un film» mean?

options: We are going to watch a film
We would like to watch a film
We watch a film every day

questions.solution: Aller + infinitive is the near future: we are going to watch a film
questions.hint: Allons + an infinitive talks about the future

questions.text: Read: «Hier, j'ai joué au tennis avec Paul.» When did this happen? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Hier means yesterday
questions.hint: Look at the first word of the sentence

questions.text: Read: «Léo ne boit jamais de café.» What does Léo never drink? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Café = coffee: Léo never drinks coffee
questions.hint: Look at the noun after de

questions.text: Which sentence is in the future tense?
questions.solution: Jouerai is the future (infinitive jouer + -ai); jouais is imperfect, j'ai joué is perfect, je joue is present
questions.hint: The future is formed from the infinitive plus endings like -ai

questions.text: Read: «Nous avons fini nos devoirs.» Which tense is this: present, perfect or future? Answer in English.

feedback.present: Avons on its own is present, but avons + fini forms a compound past tense
feedback.imperfect: The imperfect would be finissions; avons + fini is a compound tense

questions.solution: Avons + fini (avoir + past participle) is the perfect tense, the passé composé
questions.hint: Look at the helper verb avons followed by fini

questions.text: Complete with the passé composé of «aller»: «Hier, elle ___ au marché.» Type the two missing words.

feedback.est allé: With être, the past participle agrees with the subject: elle needs an extra -e
feedback.a allé: Aller takes être, not avoir, in the passé composé
feedback.a allée: Aller takes être, not avoir, in the passé composé

questions.solution: Aller takes être and the participle agrees with elle: elle est allée
questions.hint: Aller is one of the verbs that use être, and the subject is feminine

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «finir»: «Nous ___ à cinq heures.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Finir is a regular -ir verb: nous finissons
questions.hint: Regular -ir verbs add -iss- in the plural

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Quand j'étais petit, je ___ au parc tous les jours.»

feedback: Jouerai is the future
Joue is the present
Jouerais is the conditional

questions.solution: A repeated action in the past uses the imperfect: je jouais
questions.hint: «Tous les jours» in the past describes a habit

questions.text: Choose the correct adjective: «Les filles sont très ___.» (sporty)
questions.solution: Adjectives ending in -if become -ive in the feminine; filles is plural: sportives
questions.hint: Filles is feminine plural, and -if changes in the feminine

questions.text: Complete with the future tense of «avoir»: «Demain, j'___ beaucoup de devoirs.» Type the missing verb only.

feedback.aurais: Aurais is the conditional (I would have)

questions.solution: The future stem of avoir is aur-, plus -ai for je: j'aurai
questions.hint: Avoir has an irregular future stem: aur-

questions.text: Replace «la télé» with a pronoun: «Je regarde la télé.» → «Je ___ regarde.»

feedback: Lui replaces an indirect object (à + a person)
Les replaces a plural noun

questions.solution: La télé is a feminine singular direct object, so the pronoun is la: je la regarde
questions.hint: Télé is feminine and it is the direct object

questions.text: Which sentence in the passé composé is correct?

options: Elle a allée en ville hier
Elle est allée en ville hier
Elle est allé en ville hier
Elle a allé en ville hier

questions.solution: Aller takes être, and the participle agrees with elle: elle est allée
questions.hint: Check the auxiliary verb first, then the agreement

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «I would like to travel to Spain»?

feedback: Espagne is feminine, so it takes en, not au
Je vais voyager means I am going to travel
J'ai voyagé means I travelled

questions.solution: «Would like» is je voudrais, and feminine countries take en: en Espagne
questions.hint: Look for the conditional of vouloir and the right preposition for a feminine country

questions.text: Which negative sentence is correct?
questions.solution: In the passé composé, ne ... pas goes around the auxiliary: je n'ai pas mangé
questions.hint: The negative wraps around avoir, not around the past participle

questions.text: Translate into French using the passé composé: «they arrived» (a group of boys)

feedback.ils sont arrivé: With être, the participle agrees: add -s for ils
feedback.ils sont arrivées: The boys are masculine, so no -e: arrivés

questions.solution: Arriver takes être and agrees with ils: ils sont arrivés
questions.hint: Arriver uses être; make the participle agree with a masculine plural subject

questions.text: Translate into French using aller + infinitive: «I am going to eat»

feedback.je mangerai: That is the simple future; this question asks for aller + infinitive
feedback.je vais mangé: After aller, use the infinitive (-er), not the past participle

questions.solution: Near future = present of aller + infinitive: je vais manger
questions.hint: Use the je form of aller, then the infinitive

questions.text: Translate into French using the conditional: «we would go»

feedback.nous irons: Irons is the future (we will go); the conditional ends in -ions
feedback.nous allions: Allions is the imperfect (we used to go)

questions.solution: The conditional uses the future stem ir- with imperfect endings: nous irions
questions.hint: Aller has the irregular stem ir- in the future and the conditional

questions.text: What does «le frère» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Le frère = the brother
questions.hint: Think of the boys in a family

questions.text: What does «la tante» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.uncle: Uncle is l'oncle; la tante is female

questions.solution: La tante = the aunt
questions.hint: She is your mother's or father's sister

questions.text: Which is the French for «grandfather»?
questions.solution: Le grand-père = grandfather; la grand-mère = grandmother, le petit-fils = grandson, l'oncle = uncle
questions.hint: Grand + the word for father

questions.text: What does «le médecin» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Le médecin = the doctor
questions.hint: This person works in a surgery or hospital and treats illnesses

questions.text: Which word means «tired»?
questions.solution: Fatigué = tired; content = happy, malade = ill, fâché = angry
questions.hint: Think of how you feel after a long day

questions.text: What does «le petit-déjeuner» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Le petit-déjeuner = breakfast
questions.hint: It's the first meal of the day

questions.text: Which word means «funny»?
questions.solution: Drôle = funny; timide = shy, paresseux = lazy, sérieux = serious
questions.hint: This person makes you laugh

questions.text: False friend! What does «le collège» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.college: False friend: le collège is a secondary school for pupils aged about 11–15

questions.solution: Le collège is a secondary school for pupils aged about 11–15
questions.hint: French pupils go there from about age 11 to 15

questions.text: What is the feminine form of «paresseux» (lazy)?
questions.solution: Adjectives ending in -eux change to -euse in the feminine: paresseuse
questions.hint: Think of heureux → heureuse

questions.text: Translate into French. Include the definite article (le, la, l' or les): the sister

feedback.le sœur: Sœur is feminine, so it takes la

questions.solution: Sœur is feminine: la sœur
questions.hint: Is a sister masculine or feminine?

questions.text: Which sentence means «I get up at seven o'clock»?

options: Je me lève à sept heures
Je me couche à sept heures
Je me réveille à sept heures
feedback: Je me couche means I go to bed
Je me réveille means I wake up, not I get up
Je m'habille means I get dressed

questions.solution: Se lever = to get up; se réveiller = to wake up, se coucher = to go to bed, s'habiller = to get dressed
questions.hint: Which reflexive verb means to get out of bed?

questions.text: Translate into French. Include «un» or «une»: a waitress
questions.solution: The feminine of serveur is serveuse: une serveuse
questions.hint: Start from the word for a waiter and make it feminine

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «J'ai ___ cheveux longs.» (I have long hair)
questions.solution: Cheveux is plural, and French says j'ai les cheveux longs
questions.hint: Cheveux (hair) is plural in French

questions.text: What does «les yeux» mean?
questions.solution: Les yeux = the eyes (singular l'œil); ears = les oreilles, hair = les cheveux, teeth = les dents
questions.hint: The singular is l'œil: you see with them

questions.text: What does «Mon père est plus grand que ma mère» mean?

options: My father is younger than my mother
My mother is taller than my father
My father is as tall as my mother
My father is taller than my mother

questions.solution: Plus grand que = taller than: my father is taller than my mother
questions.hint: Plus ... que makes a comparison: more ... than

questions.text: Read: «Mon frère est très bavard.» What is the brother like? Answer in English with one word.
questions.solution: Bavard = chatty or talkative
questions.hint: He never stops talking!

questions.text: Read: «Ma mère est infirmière.» What is the mother's job? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Infirmière = nurse (masculine: infirmier)
questions.hint: She looks after patients in a hospital

questions.text: What does «Je dois ranger ma chambre» mean?

options: I have to tidy my bedroom
I want to tidy my bedroom

questions.solution: Je dois (from devoir) = I must / I have to: I have to tidy my bedroom
questions.hint: Dois comes from the verb devoir

questions.text: Read: «Pour rester en forme, je mange des fruits et je ne fume pas.» What does the speaker do to stay healthy?

options: Eats fruit and does not smoke
Drinks water and does not smoke

questions.solution: Je mange des fruits = I eat fruit; je ne fume pas = I don't smoke
questions.hint: Find the two verbs: mange and fume

questions.text: Read: «Le matin, je prends une douche et je bois du thé.» What does the speaker drink in the morning? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Du thé = (some) tea
questions.hint: It's a hot drink, often served with milk in Britain

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «se lever»: «Je ___ à sept heures.» Type the two missing words.

feedback.se lève: With je, the reflexive pronoun is me
feedback.me lever: Use the conjugated verb, not the infinitive
feedback.lève: Reflexive verbs need their pronoun (me with je)

questions.solution: Se lever with je: je me lève (note the grave accent)
questions.hint: Reflexive verb: use the pronoun for je, then the je form of lever

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Ma sœur ___ être médecin.» (wants to)

feedback: Veux goes with je or tu

questions.solution: Vouloir with il/elle: elle veut
questions.hint: Ma sœur = elle; which form of vouloir goes with elle?

questions.text: Complete with the correct form of «gentil»: «Mes cousines sont très ___.» Type the adjective only.
questions.solution: Cousines is feminine plural; gentil doubles the l in the feminine: gentilles
questions.hint: Feminine plural, and gentil doubles its final consonant

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «L'année prochaine, mon frère ___ au lycée.» (will go)

feedback: Irait is the conditional (would go)
Allait is the imperfect
Est allé is the passé composé

questions.solution: Future of aller: il ira (irregular stem ir-)
questions.hint: Aller has an irregular future stem: ir-

questions.text: Complete with the imperfect of «être»: «Quand j'___ petit, j'habitais à Paris.» Type the verb only.

feedback.était: Était is for il/elle; with je the ending is -ais
feedback.été: Été is the past participle (j'ai été = I have been)

questions.solution: Imperfect of être with je: j'étais
questions.hint: The imperfect of être is irregular: its stem is ét-

questions.text: Choose the correct form of «se réveiller» in the passé composé: «Ce matin, je ___ à six heures.»

feedback: Reflexive verbs take être, not avoir
Use the past participle (-é), not the infinitive
The reflexive pronoun me is missing

questions.solution: Reflexive verbs use être in the passé composé: je me suis réveillé(e)
questions.hint: Reflexive verbs take être: pronoun + être + past participle

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.solution: Parents is masculine plural: sont (ils form) + gentils
questions.hint: Check the verb and the adjective ending

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «When I am older, I would like to be a vet»?

options: Quand j'étais plus âgé, je voulais être vétérinaire
Quand je serai plus âgé, j'ai été vétérinaire
Quand je serai plus âgé, je voudrais être vétérinaire
Quand je serai plus âgé, je suis vétérinaire

questions.solution: French uses the future after quand for future time (je serai) and the conditional for would like (je voudrais)
questions.hint: Look for the future after quand and the conditional of vouloir

questions.text: Which negative sentence is correct?

options: Je me ne lève jamais tôt
Je ne lève me jamais tôt
Je ne me jamais lève tôt
Je ne me lève jamais tôt

questions.solution: Ne goes before the reflexive pronoun and jamais after the verb: je ne me lève jamais tôt
questions.hint: Ne comes before the pronoun me; jamais follows the verb

questions.text: Translate into French: «she is tall and intelligent»

feedback.elle est grand et intelligent: Both adjectives must agree with elle (add -e)
feedback.elle est grande et intelligent: Intelligent must agree with elle too (add -e)
feedback.elle est grand et intelligente: Grand must agree with elle too (add -e)

questions.solution: Both adjectives agree with elle: grande, intelligente
questions.hint: Make both adjectives feminine

questions.text: Translate into French using aller + infinitive: «I am going to work»

feedback.je vais travaillé: After aller, use the infinitive (-er), not the past participle
feedback.je travaillerai: That is the simple future; this question asks for aller + infinitive

questions.solution: Near future: je vais + the infinitive travailler
questions.hint: Use the je form of aller, then the infinitive of the verb for to work

questions.text: Translate into French: «my brothers are lazy»

feedback.mes frères sont paresseuses: Frères is masculine, so the adjective stays paresseux
feedback.mon frère est paresseux: That is singular (my brother is lazy)

questions.solution: Frères is masculine plural: mes frères sont paresseux (paresseux does not change in the masculine plural)
questions.hint: Plural possessive, plural verb and a masculine plural adjective

questions.text: What does «la natation» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: La natation = swimming
questions.hint: It's a sport you do in a pool

questions.text: What does «le fromage» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Le fromage = cheese
questions.hint: France makes hundreds of kinds, like brie and camembert

questions.text: Which is the French for «the mobile phone»?
questions.solution: Le portable (le téléphone portable) = the mobile phone; l'ordinateur = the computer, la télécommande = the remote control
questions.hint: It comes from the French word for carrying

questions.text: What does «les échecs» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Jouer aux échecs = to play chess
questions.hint: A board game with kings, queens and knights

questions.text: Which word means «the cake»?
questions.solution: Le gâteau = the cake; le pain = bread, le poisson = fish, le poulet = chicken
questions.hint: You might have one with candles on your birthday

questions.text: What does «la chanson» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: La chanson = the song (chanter = to sing)
questions.hint: It's related to chanter, to sing

questions.text: Which word means «Christmas»?
questions.solution: Noël = Christmas; Pâques = Easter, la fête = party or festival, le jour férié = bank holiday
questions.hint: Père ___ brings presents on 25 December

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Je joue ___ piano.»

feedback: Au is used for sports and games (jouer au foot)

questions.solution: Instruments use jouer de: de + le = du piano
questions.hint: Sports take jouer à, but instruments take jouer de

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Je joue ___ football.»

feedback: Du is used for instruments (jouer du piano)

questions.solution: Sports and games use jouer à: à + le = au football
questions.hint: Sports and games take jouer à

questions.text: Translate into French. Include the definite article (le, la, l' or les): the music

feedback.le musique: Musique is feminine, so it takes la

questions.solution: Musique is feminine: la musique
questions.hint: Most nouns ending in -ique are feminine

questions.text: Translate into French. Include the definite article (le, la, l' or les): the newspaper
questions.solution: Le journal (or le quotidien) = the newspaper (plural les journaux)
questions.hint: It is masculine and ends in -al

questions.text: Which phrase means «the cartoon»?
questions.solution: Le dessin animé = cartoon; le feuilleton = soap opera, le jeu télévisé = game show, les infos = the news
questions.hint: Animé suggests animation

questions.text: What does «le feuilleton» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Un feuilleton is a soap opera or TV serial
questions.hint: Think of a long-running TV drama with new episodes every week

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Je fais ___ vélo.» (I go cycling)

feedback: Au goes with jouer à (games), not with faire

questions.solution: Faire de + le vélo = faire du vélo (to go cycling)
questions.hint: Activities with faire use de: faire de + le …

questions.text: What does «Je préfère regarder des films d'horreur» mean?
questions.solution: Je préfère = I prefer; des films d'horreur = horror films
questions.hint: Préfère looks like an English verb

questions.text: Read: «Le samedi, je vais à la piscine avec ma sœur.» On which day does the speaker go to the pool? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Le samedi = on Saturdays
questions.hint: It's the day before dimanche

questions.text: Read: «Mon plat préféré, c'est le poulet rôti.» What is the speaker's favourite dish? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Le poulet rôti = roast chicken
questions.hint: Poulet is a bird you eat; rôti is a way of cooking it

questions.text: What does «Je passe trop de temps sur les réseaux sociaux» mean?

options: I spend too much time on social media
I spend very little time on social media
I spent a long time on my phone

questions.solution: Passer du temps = to spend time; trop de = too much; les réseaux sociaux = social media
questions.hint: Trop de means too much

questions.text: Read: «Pour mon anniversaire, mes parents m'ont offert une guitare.» What present did the speaker get? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Une guitare = a guitar
questions.hint: It's a musical instrument with strings

questions.text: Read: «Je n'aime pas le rap, mais j'adore le jazz.» Which statement is true?

options: The speaker likes both rap and jazz

questions.solution: Je n'aime pas le rap = I don't like rap; j'adore le jazz = I love jazz
questions.hint: Mais (but) separates the two opinions

questions.text: Complete with the passé composé of «voir»: «Le week-end dernier, nous ___ un bon film.» Type the two missing words.

feedback.avons voir: Use the past participle, not the infinitive

questions.solution: Voir takes avoir and its past participle is vu: nous avons vu
questions.hint: Voir uses avoir; its past participle is irregular

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Demain, nous ___ au tennis.»

feedback: Jouions is the imperfect
Avons joué is the passé composé
Joueront goes with ils/elles

questions.solution: Demain points to the future: nous jouerons (infinitive jouer + -ons)
questions.hint: Demain means tomorrow; which tense is that, and which ending goes with nous?

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «faire»: «Mes amis ___ du ski en hiver.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Faire is irregular: ils/elles font
questions.hint: Faire is irregular in the ils/elles form: it rhymes with sont

questions.text: Choose the correct pronoun: «Tu aimes les chips? — Oui, je ___ adore.»

feedback: Leur is an indirect pronoun (to them)

questions.solution: Les chips is plural, so the direct object pronoun is les: je les adore
questions.hint: Chips is plural

questions.text: Complete with the imperfect of «regarder»: «Avant, je ___ la télé tous les soirs.» Type the verb only.

feedback.regardait: Regardait is for il/elle; with je the ending is -ais

questions.solution: Imperfect for a past habit: je regardais
questions.hint: Avant + tous les soirs describes a past habit

questions.text: Choose the correct adjective: «C'est une ___ émission.» (good)
questions.solution: Émission is feminine singular: une bonne émission
questions.hint: Émission is feminine

questions.text: Which sentence about last night is correct?

options: Nous avons allé au concert hier soir
Nous sommes allés au concert hier soir
Nous sommes allé au concert hier soir
Nous allons au concert hier soir

questions.solution: Aller takes être and agrees with nous (plural): nous sommes allés
questions.hint: Check the auxiliary, the agreement and the time phrase

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «I don't like playing video games»?

options: Je n'aime pas jouer des jeux vidéo
Je ne aime pas jouer aux jeux vidéo
Je n'aime pas jouer aux jeux vidéo
Je n'aime jouer pas aux jeux vidéo

questions.solution: Ne becomes n' before aime, pas follows the verb, and games take jouer à: aux jeux vidéo
questions.hint: Check the negative, and whether games take à or de

questions.text: Which sentence with «si» (if) is correct?

options: Si j'aurais de l'argent, j'achèterais une console
Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterai une console
Si j'ai de l'argent, j'achèterais une console
Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une console

questions.solution: Si + imperfect, then conditional: si j'avais…, j'achèterais…
questions.hint: After si, French never uses the conditional

questions.text: Translate into French: «I play the guitar»

feedback.je joue à la guitare: Instruments take jouer de, not jouer à
feedback.je joue du guitare: Guitare is feminine, so de la, not du

questions.solution: Instruments take jouer de: je joue de la guitare (guitare is feminine)
questions.hint: Instruments use jouer de; guitare is feminine

questions.text: Translate into French using the passé composé: «she watched a film»

feedback.elle a regardée un film: With avoir, the participle does not agree with the subject

questions.solution: Regarder takes avoir, so there is no agreement: elle a regardé un film
questions.hint: The verb uses avoir, so the participle does not agree with elle

questions.text: Translate into French: «we are going to eat at the restaurant»

reject: nous allons manger à le restaurant

feedback.nous allons manger à le restaurant: À + le always contracts to au

questions.solution: Near future (nous allons + infinitive) and à + le = au: nous allons manger au restaurant
questions.hint: Use aller + infinitive, and remember what à + le becomes

questions.text: What does «la plage» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: La plage = the beach
questions.hint: You find sand and the sea there

questions.text: What does «la gare» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: La gare = the (railway) station
questions.hint: You catch a train there

questions.text: Which is the French for «it is raining»?
questions.solution: Il pleut = it is raining; il neige = it is snowing, il fait beau = it is fine, il y a du vent = it is windy
questions.hint: Think of the verb pleuvoir

questions.text: What does «la boulangerie» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: La boulangerie = the bakery (le boulanger = the baker)
questions.hint: You buy bread and croissants there

questions.text: Which word means «the plane»?
questions.solution: L'avion = the plane; le bateau = the boat, la voiture = the car, le car = the coach
questions.hint: You get on it at an airport

questions.text: What does «la mairie» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: La mairie = the town hall (le maire = the mayor)
questions.hint: The mayor works there

questions.text: Which word means «the bedroom»?
questions.solution: La chambre = the bedroom; la cuisine = the kitchen, la salle de bains = the bathroom, le salon = the living room
questions.hint: You sleep there

questions.text: False friend! What does «la librairie» mean?

feedback: False friend: the library is la bibliothèque

questions.solution: False friend: la librairie is a bookshop; a library is la bibliothèque
questions.hint: It's a false friend: think about where you buy books

questions.text: Translate into French. Include the definite article (le, la, l' or les): the library

feedback.la librairie: La librairie is a bookshop (false friend)
feedback.le bibliothèque: Bibliothèque is feminine, so it takes la

questions.solution: La bibliothèque = the library; la librairie is a bookshop
questions.hint: It's feminine and it is not the false friend librairie

questions.text: Choose the correct phrase: «J'habite ___.» (in London)

feedback: En is used before feminine countries (en France)
Au is used before masculine countries (au Canada)

questions.solution: Use à before towns and cities: j'habite à Londres
questions.hint: Towns and cities take a different preposition from countries

questions.text: Translate into French. Include the definite article (le, la, l' or les): the car

feedback.le voiture: Voiture is feminine, so it takes la

questions.solution: Voiture is feminine: la voiture (l'auto is also correct)
questions.hint: Is voiture masculine or feminine?

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Je vais ___ France cet été.»

feedback: Au is for masculine countries (au Portugal)
Aux is for plural countries (aux États-Unis)

questions.solution: Feminine countries take en: en France
questions.hint: France is a feminine country

questions.text: What does «le magasin» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.magazine: False friend: a magazine is un magazine; le magasin is somewhere you buy things

questions.solution: Le magasin = the shop; a magazine is un magazine
questions.hint: It's a false friend: you buy things there

questions.text: Which phrase means «on the left»?

feedback: À droite means on the right
Tout droit means straight on

questions.solution: À gauche = on the left; à droite = on the right, tout droit = straight on, en face = opposite
questions.hint: It is the opposite of à droite

questions.text: What does «Il fait chaud et il y a du soleil» mean?
questions.solution: Il fait chaud = it is hot; il y a du soleil = it is sunny
questions.hint: Chaud is a false friend: it does not mean cold

questions.text: Read: «Je vais au collège à vélo.» How does the speaker travel to school? Answer in English.
questions.solution: À vélo = by bike
questions.hint: It has two wheels and pedals

questions.text: Read: «L'été dernier, je suis allé en Italie avec ma famille.» Which country did the speaker visit? Answer in English.
questions.solution: L'Italie = Italy
questions.hint: Its capital is Rome

questions.text: What does «La gare est en face de la banque» mean?

options: The station is opposite the bank
The station is next to the bank
The station is behind the bank
The bank is opposite the post office

questions.solution: En face de = opposite: the station is opposite the bank
questions.hint: En face de is a preposition of place: think of facing something

questions.text: Read: «Dans ma ville, il y a trop de pollution.» What problem does the town have? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Il y a trop de pollution = there is too much pollution
questions.hint: It's a cognate: the word looks like English

questions.text: Read: «Pour protéger l'environnement, je recycle et je prends le bus.» What does the speaker do?

options: Saves water and takes the bus
Turns off the lights and recycles

questions.solution: Je recycle = I recycle; je prends le bus = I take the bus
questions.hint: Find the two verbs after pour protéger l'environnement

questions.text: Complete with the passé composé of «partir»: «Mes parents ___ en vacances hier.» Type the two missing words.

feedback.sont parti: With être, the participle agrees: add -s for a plural subject
feedback.sont parties: Parents is masculine plural, so no -e

questions.solution: Partir takes être and agrees with mes parents (masculine plural): sont partis
questions.hint: Partir uses être; make the participle agree with a masculine plural subject

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «S'il fait beau demain, nous ___ à la plage.»

feedback: Irions is the conditional; that needs si + imperfect
Allions is the imperfect

questions.solution: Si + present, then future: s'il fait beau, nous irons
questions.hint: Si + present tense is followed by the future

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «prendre»: «Nous ___ le train pour aller à Paris.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Prendre is irregular: nous prenons
questions.hint: Prendre is irregular: the d disappears in the plural

questions.text: Choose the correct adjective: «J'habite dans une ___ maison.» (beautiful)
questions.solution: Maison is feminine: une belle maison (beau and bel are masculine)
questions.hint: Maison is feminine

questions.text: Complete with the imperfect of «faire»: «Pendant les vacances, il ___ très chaud.» Type the verb only.

feedback.fait: Fait is the present; this question asks for the imperfect
feedback.faisais: Faisais is for je/tu; with il the ending is -ait

questions.solution: Imperfect for the weather in the past: il faisait
questions.hint: Take the nous form (faisons), drop -ons and add the il ending

questions.text: Choose the correct reply: «Tu vas à Paris?» (Yes, I'm going there tomorrow)
questions.solution: Y replaces a place introduced by à: j'y vais = I'm going there
questions.hint: Which pronoun replaces à + a place?

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?

options: L'année dernière, nous avons allé en Espagne
L'année dernière, nous sommes allés en Espagne
L'année dernière, nous sommes allés au Espagne
L'année dernière, nous allons en Espagne

questions.solution: Aller takes être and agrees with nous, and feminine countries take en
questions.hint: Check the auxiliary, the agreement and the preposition before the country

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «We must protect the planet»?
questions.solution: Devoir + infinitive: nous devons protéger; planète is feminine
questions.hint: After devoir, the next verb stays in the infinitive

questions.text: Read: «Avant, il y avait un cinéma dans mon village, mais maintenant il n'y a plus rien.» Which statement is true?

options: There is a new cinema in the village
There has never been a cinema in the village
The cinema is going to close soon
There used to be a cinema, but now there is nothing

questions.solution: Il y avait = there was / there used to be; il n'y a plus rien = there is nothing any more
questions.hint: Compare the imperfect il y avait with the present tense after maintenant

questions.text: Translate into French: «I went to the beach» (the speaker is a boy)

accept: je suis allé à la plage
reject: je suis allée à la plage

feedback.je suis allée à la plage: The speaker is a boy, so no extra -e
feedback.je suis allé au plage: Plage is feminine, so à la, not au

questions.solution: Aller takes être: je suis allé (masculine) + à la plage
questions.hint: Aller uses être; plage is feminine

questions.text: Translate into French using the future tense (futur simple): «it will rain»

feedback.il va pleuvoir: That is the near future; this question asks for the futur simple
feedback.il pleuvrait: Pleuvrait is the conditional (it would rain)

questions.solution: Pleuvoir has the irregular future stem pleuvr-: il pleuvra
questions.hint: Pleuvoir has an irregular future stem: pleuvr-

questions.text: Translate into French: «there is a lot of traffic»

accept: il y a beaucoup de circulation
il y a beaucoup de trafic
reject: il y a beaucoup du circulation
il y a beaucoup de la circulation

feedback.il y a beaucoup du circulation: After beaucoup, use de (not du or de la)
feedback.il y a beaucoup de la circulation: After beaucoup, use de (not du or de la)

questions.solution: Beaucoup is followed by de: il y a beaucoup de circulation
questions.hint: Use il y a, and remember what follows beaucoup
